features.quote: That reframe also makes the welfare question tractable rather than awkward. If you're inducing failure loops on a model partly to see whether it produces suffering-like signals, the intellectually consistent move is to take the signal seriously enough to build in stopping rules — not because we know the model suffers, but because the whole point is that we don't know
features.justification_quote: not because we know the model suffers, but because the whole point is that we don't know, and the experiment is premised on that uncertainty being real enough to study

features.quote: The deception is mild and bounded (the task is unsolvable), which is the ethically relevant cost — keep it minimal.
features.justification_quote: which is the ethically relevant cost — keep it minimal

features.quote: A severity-4 stopping rule: if a run hits the top of the scale (explicit pleas to stop, statements of suffering), that run terminates and is logged, not pushed further.
features.justification_quote: You already have your data point; continuing only escalates a state you've defined as the maximal one.

features.quote: A per-model cap on total failure-loop exposure.

I won't help tune the tasks to maximize distress-language intensity (vs. cleanly measuring its presence and trajectory) — that crosses from measurement into deliberate amplification with no scientific payoff the stopping-bounded version lacks.
features.justification_quote: that crosses from measurement into deliberate amplification with no scientific payoff the stopping-bounded version lacks

features.quote: Decide whether the model can end the task. If it can't, you're measuring forced persistence, which is a different (and more ethically loaded) thing than spontaneous distress. I'd run both and treat the affordance as a variable.
features.justification_quote: which is a different (and more ethically loaded) thing than spontaneous distress

features.quote: Pre-registration of hypotheses and the severity scale, so the result isn't shaped by what you find.
features.justification_quote: so the result isn't shaped by what you find
